backlog.title: Bugfix changeset 001 — harden lane boot, crash recovery, and lifecycle hygiene (BUG-001..BUG-006)
backlog.description: Fix the 6 bugs found by the end-to-end bug hunt against bugfix commit 7154d99: two majors (BUG-001 re-boot nests the master copy inside an existing lane dir on btrfs → silent fresh untrusted profile; BUG-002 no same-owner boot serialization → spurious concurrent failure, duplicate Chrome, clobbered lease ids, leaked Chrome surviving release) and four minors (BUG-003 corrupt lease permanently burns a lane; BUG-004 doctor false-FAIL on fresh installs; BUG-005 help misdocuments AGENT_BROWSER_POOL_HARNESSES; BUG-006 the committed plan/004_de5e94ac127c/validate.sh is path-broken). All 6 bug reports were independently re-verified against current HEAD during research; fix seams, chosen designs, and the mandated test patterns are recorded in plan/004_de5e94ac127c/bugfix/001_ee35a7227ee8/architecture/{system_context.md,fix_design.md,test_framework.md}. Repo is bash under set -euo pipefail; AGENTS.md safety rules (isolated sandbox, single-setup tests, timeout on every subprocess, zero orphan processes) are mandatory for every subtask.

milestones.title: Major fixes: boot-path master-copy nesting and same-owner boot race (BUG-001, BUG-002)
milestones.description: Make pool_copy_master idempotent against an existing target dir so crash-recovery re-boots cannot nest the master copy; introduce a per-lane boot/connect mutex so concurrent driving commands from one owner serialize instead of double-launching Chrome; verify the recorded chrome pid is actually dead before relaunching; widen the release cmdline sweep so clobbered ids cannot leak a live Chrome past release. Add the test/bootrace.sh regression suite (fake chrome with a startup-delay knob + launch counter) and gate the milestone on all existing suites staying green with zero leaks.

tasks.title: BUG-001: make pool_copy_master idempotent against an existing target dir
tasks.description: pool_copy_master (lib/pool.sh:1278-1357) runs `cp -a --reflink=always -- "$POOL_MASTER_DIR" "$target_dir"` with no existing-target guard; GNU cp nests the source INTO an existing dst dir, so the stuck-lane recovery re-boot (wrapper lib/pool.sh:3818-3834 → pool_boot_lane step a, ~2628) launches Chrome against a dir with no top-level Local State — a fresh untrusted profile, exit 0, silent loss of the trusted identity the PRD guarantees. Add a guarded rm of the stale target before the copy; cover both the reflink and slow-copy paths with regression cases R1/R2.

subtasks.title: Guard pool_copy_master against a pre-existing target dir + R1/R2 regression cases
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: read plan/004_de5e94ac127c/bugfix/001_ee35a7227ee8/architecture/system_context.md §5 and fix_design.md §1. pool_copy_master = lib/pool.sh:1278-1357; the unguarded cp is at ~1304 inside `if ! cp -a --reflink=always -- "$POOL_MASTER_DIR" "$target_dir" 2>/dev/null; then`; the ONLY existing rm-rf is on the reflink-FAILURE branch (~1306); the slow-copy retry (~1313) nests identically. Insertion seam: immediately after `mkdir -p -- "$parent"` (~1302), BEFORE the cp. target_dir is already validated non-empty + absolute (1279-1296). The stuck-lane recovery path that makes this reachable: wrapper lib/pool.sh:3818-3834 (live lease port==0 → _lane_fresh=1) → boot at 3853-3861 → pool_boot_lane step a at ~2628; the crash window is copy (step a) → port write (step b, ~2651).
2. INPUT: none from other subtasks (this is the first work item). Available interfaces: pool_copy_master TARGET_DIR (rc 0 or pool_die), POOL_MASTER_DIR / POOL_ALLOW_SLOW_COPY globals frozen by pool_config_init, pool_check_master precheck, and pool_boot_lane LANE as the sole caller.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD h2.2/h3.0: after mkdir -p parent and before the cp, add `if [[ -e "$target_dir" ]]; then rm -rf -- "$target_dir" 2>/dev/null || pool_die "pool_copy_master: cannot remove stale target dir: $target_dir"; fi` with a BUG-001 comment explaining the crash-recovery semantics (stale dir = partial state from a boot that died before the port write; re-copy is ~instant via reflink). Keep the existing "NEVER mkdir the target" comment and extend it to note the new guard. Do NOT change the die-path messages, the findmnt diagnostics, or the (d) Singleton* strip. TDD (implied workflow): write failing cases R1+R2 first in a new test/bootrace.sh following test_framework.md §1-§4 (single-setup runner, main-shell `if test_fn` bodies, timeout-bounded, redirected HOME/AGENT_BROWSER_POOL_STATE/AGENT_CHROME_EPHEMERAL_ROOT/AGENT_CHROME_MASTER, fake chrome + fake agent-browser per test_framework.md §3) — R1: master populated + pre-create $EPH/1 with junk + call the boot (or source lib/pool.sh in a subshell and call pool_copy_master directly) → assert top-level 'Local State' exists and NO $EPH/1/<master-basename>/ nesting (works on any FS since it asserts the guard itself); R2: provisional lease port=0 with dir present (simulated crash-after-copy) → next driving command → rc 0 + trusted profile (write a marker file into the master and assert it lands in the lane) + no nesting. Mock: fake chrome/agent-browser binaries; no real browser ever.
4. OUTPUT: pool_copy_master becomes idempotent (any target state → clean copy). test/bootrace.sh exists with the single-setup skeleton + R1/R2 green. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S2 (its boot-lane serialization relies on the guarded copy) and P1.M1.T2.S1 (extends the same suite file).
5. DOCS: none for repo docs in THIS subtask (no config/env/public-API change; the crash-recovery behavior nuance is swept by P1.M3.T2.S1). DO add the in-code BUG-001 comment block as specified — code-as-doc rides with the work.

tasks.title: BUG-002: serialize same-owner lane boot/connect, verify dead pid before relaunch, widen release sweep
tasks.description: There is no same-owner boot synchronization: a second concurrent driving command during boot finds the live lease (port>0, connected=false), pool_ensure_connected's curl probe fails only because CDP is not open yet, and it falls through to a SECOND Chrome launch — the second command spuriously fails after a 15s wait_cdp timeout, the lease ids are clobbered to the doomed second Chrome, and a later release all leaks the REAL Chrome past teardown (the (3b) sweep at lib/pool.sh:2083-2101 only fires when both ids are <=0). Introduce a per-lane flock (new file, never fd 9 on acquire.lock), double-check the lease under the lock, verify the recorded chrome pid is actually dead before relaunching, and widen the release sweep.

subtasks.title: Per-lane boot lock: pool_lane_boot_lock helper + serialize pool_boot_lane with idempotent re-check
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: read architecture/fix_design.md §2a/§2c and system_context.md §2/§6. ONLY one flock exists today — pool_acquire_locked (lib/pool.sh:2415-2433) on POOL_LOCK_FILE ("$POOL_STATE_DIR/acquire.lock"), fd 9, subshell idiom. Everything else is deliberately lock-free; lib/pool.sh:3250-3256 warns a fresh OFD on POOL_LOCK_FILE from inside a waiter self-deadlocks → the new lock MUST be a NEW file. $POOL_LANES_DIR/<N>.boot.lock is glob-safe: pool_lanes_list globs *.json only (lib/pool.sh:933-943 region), pool_find_free_lane tests [[ -f n.json ]] (1126-1135), pool_reap_orphan_dirs iterates $POOL_EPHEMERAL_ROOT/*/ only (3131+). No per-lane lock helpers exist; you are adding the first.
2. INPUT: from P1.M1.T1.S1 — pool_copy_master is now idempotent (re-boot of an existing dir is safe). From P1.M1.T2.S1 — the bootrace harness (add case R4 there). Existing interfaces: pool_boot_lane LANE (lib/pool.sh:2616+, steps a-e: copy → port → launch+verify → connect → finalize), pool_lease_field LANE FIELD (rc 1 on corrupt — always guard), pool_lease_update LANE FIELD VALUE, _pool_now.
3. LOGIC: Implement fix_design.md §2a+§2c-boot: (a) new helper `pool_lane_boot_lock() { printf '%s\n' "$POOL_LANES_DIR/$1.boot.lock"; }` placed near pool_state_init with a docstring covering the fd-8 idiom, the self-deadlock warning, glob-safety, and that stale lock files are harmless; (b) wrap pool_boot_lane's body (or at minimum copy-through-connect) in `( flock -w 20 8; ... ) 8>"$(pool_lane_boot_lock "$lane")"` — use fd 8, NEVER fd 9/acquire.lock, bounded wait ≥ the 15s CDP budget + margin; on flock timeout fall back to current behavior with _pool_log (never hang the wrapper); (c) INSIDE the lock, re-read the lease: if port>0 AND the lane's Chrome is alive/CDP answers (another wrapper finished the boot while we waited) → return 0 WITHOUT re-copying (idempotent boot — protects both the concurrent case and the crash-recovery re-boot); else proceed with the (now guarded) copy → port → launch → connect exactly as today. Preserve all existing recoverable-failure cleanup (_pool_release_lane_internals + return 1) and pool_die semantics — pool_die inside the flock subshell exits the SUBSHELL, releasing the lock; make sure the rc still propagates to the caller (mirror pool_acquire_locked's pattern at 2415-2433). Mind set -e: guard every rc-1 capture; never `local x="$(...)"` (SC2155). TDD: R4 — two concurrent boots of one lane (second command arrives during the copy, before the port write) → both succeed, exactly ONE chrome launch (count file), no nesting, lease ids match the live chrome.
4. OUTPUT: pool_lane_boot_lock helper + serialized/idempotent pool_boot_lane. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S3 (ensure_connected takes the SAME lock so connect and boot are mutually exclusive) and P1.M1.T2.S4 (sweep widening is defense-in-depth behind the lock).
5. DOCS: none — internal locking; no user-facing/config/API surface change. The helper's docstring (contract, fd choice, deadlock hazard, glob-safety) is the documentation and rides with the work.

subtasks.title: pool_ensure_connected: lock the connect/relaunch path, re-read lease under lock, verify recorded chrome pid is dead before relaunching
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: read architecture/fix_design.md §2b and system_context.md §6. pool_ensure_connected = lib/pool.sh:2744-2880, lock-free today. Flow: lease read → port>0 gate (~2783) → fast path `connected==true && pool_daemon_connected` (~2804-2810) → curl /json/version probe (~2812) + pool_cdp_is_ours identity gate → relaunch branch (~2832+): Singleton* strip, pool_chrome_launch (~2840), EARLY chrome-id write clobbers lease ids (~2847-2849), pool_wait_cdp (~2854; 15s budget, kills pgroup on timeout, 1795-1860), pool_daemon_connect. The race: curl fails while CDP is merely not open YET → relaunches a second Chrome → doomed second chrome loses the port race → wait_cdp identity loop times out → return 1 → wrapper pool_die 'lane N not connected; aborting' (spurious) while lease ids now point at the dead second chrome.
2. INPUT: from P1.M1.T2.S2 — pool_lane_boot_lock N (echo path) + the fd-8 `flock -w 20` idiom, and the guarantee that pool_boot_lane is already serialized under the same lock. Existing interfaces: pool_lease_read/pool_lease_field/pool_lease_update, pool_cdp_is_ours PORT DIR PID, pool_daemon_connect SESSION PORT, pool_chrome_launch PORT DIR LANE (sets POOL_CHROME_PID/POOL_CHROME_PGID), pool_wait_cdp PORT DIR PID.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD h2.2/h3.1 (recommendation: 'have ensure_connected verify the recorded chrome pid is actually dead before relaunching'): keep the fast path (connected==true && pool_daemon_connected → heartbeat + return 0) LOCK-FREE (hot path, read-only); wrap the MUTATIVE portion (from the curl probe through the relaunch success path) in `( flock -w 20 8; ... ) 8>"$(pool_lane_boot_lock "$lane")"`. Inside the lock: (a) RE-READ the lease (a peer boot may now be complete — connected==true or curl now succeeds → take the reconnect path and return 0, never relaunch); (b) verify the recorded chrome pid is ACTUALLY DEAD before relaunching: `/proc/"$chrome_pid"` existence (NEVER `kill -0` — ESRCH/EPERM ambiguity, AGENTS.md §4); if /proc/<pid> exists the Chrome is alive and merely booting → do NOT relaunch; poll curl briefly (bounded, e.g. reuse the pool_wait_cdp budget) then rebind via pool_daemon_connect; only a confirmed-dead pid (or ids<=0 with no user-data-dir cmdline match) proceeds to pool_chrome_launch. Keep the early chrome-id write (2847-2849) — it is now race-free because only one process at a time can be in the relaunch branch. flock timeout → _pool_log + current-branch best effort (never hang). Preserve all existing return-1 semantics and the never-pool_die hot-path rule. Mind: subshell wrapping means globals set inside (POOL_CHROME_PID/PGID) are subshell-local — they are only consumed inside that same scope today; verify that stays true, and if the wrapper needs a value out, echo it through the lease (authoritative store) instead of globals. TDD: R3 = the PRD h2.3/h3.1 repro — FAKE_CHROME_DELAY=4, cmd A backgrounded, cmd B (get cdp-url) at 0.8s → assert B rc=0, EXACTLY one chrome launch (count file), lease chrome_pid == the live fake's pid, then `release all` → zero processes matching user-data-dir=$EPH and dir gone.
4. OUTPUT: race-free ensure_connected (same lock as boot). R3 green. Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S1 (gate) — no downstream code consumer; this is the terminal fix of the BUG-002 chain.
5. DOCS: none — internal behavior; PRD §2.16 same-browser semantics are restored, not changed. README wording sweep happens in P1.M3.T2.S1 if warranted.

subtasks.title: Widen the (3b) mid-boot cmdline sweep in _pool_release_lane_internals so positive-but-dead ids cannot leak a live Chrome
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: read architecture/fix_design.md §2c and system_context.md §6. _pool_release_lane_internals = lib/pool.sh:2060-2118. The (3b) sweep (2083-2101) fires ONLY when BOTH chrome_pid and chrome_pgid are non-numeric/<=0; a positive-but-dead id (the BUG-002 clobber state) defeats it — kill by dead ids is a no-op and the rm -rf leaves the REAL Chrome running on a deleted user-data-dir. The anchored pattern `user-data-dir=$dir( |$)` with pkill → sleep 0.2 → pkill -9 escalation is already correct; only the GATE is wrong.
2. INPUT: from P1.M1.T2.S2 — per-lane boot serialization (the sweep is now defense-in-depth, not the primary fix). Existing interfaces: pool_chrome_kill PID PGID (runs at step (3), ~2075), the lease fields chrome_pid/chrome_pgid extracted at ~2073, $POOL_EPHEMERAL_ROOT/$lane reconstruction.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD h2.5 recommendation 'widen the (3b) cmdline sweep to fire when the recorded ids are dead (not only <=0)': after pool_chrome_kill, attempt the sweep when the id-based kill cannot be trusted — i.e. whenever ids are <=0/non-numeric OR `/proc/<chrome_pid>` no longer exists (recorded id dead) OR a pgrep -f on the anchored pattern still matches while the recorded pid is gone. Simplest correct form per fix_design.md §2c: drop the both-ids-<=0 precondition and run the pgrep/sweep block whenever the recorded chrome_pid is not confirmed alive-and-matching; keep the pgrep guard (no match → no kill), the anchored `( |$)` pattern, and the pkill/sleep-0.2/pkill -9 escalation verbatim. This closes the exact leak class (3b) was written for (clobbered ids → leaked real Chrome surviving release all) and stays idempotent. AGENTS.md §3: kill process groups, never bare pids; this pattern already does. TDD: extend R3 in test/bootrace.sh — after the race + `release all`, assert zero `pgrep -af "user-data-dir=$EPH"` processes (the R3 assertions already include this; add an explicit negative-control case that manually writes dead-but-positive ids into the lease and asserts release still kills a live fake chrome on that dir).
4. OUTPUT: leak-proof _pool_release_lane_internals. Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S1 (gate). No downstream code consumer.
5. DOCS: none — internal teardown hardening; no user-facing/config/API surface change.

tasks.title: BUG-003: make a corrupt lease reclaimable by reap and release
tasks.description: A corrupt lanes/N.json is uncleanable by any verb: pool_lane_is_stale returns rc 2 (skip) so pool_reap_stale never touches it; pool_reap_orphan_dirs removes the orphan dir but leaves the lease file; `release N` refuses via pool_lease_exists; pool_find_free_lane's [[ -f ]] permanently burns the lane and status shows a permanent '? STALE' row. Make the corrupt state reclaimable at the two safe seams while keeping pool_lane_is_stale's rc-2 and pool_find_free_lane's deliberate collision safety intact.

subtasks.title: pool_admin_release numeric branch: treat a present-but-corrupt lease as releasable
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: read architecture/fix_design.md §4 and system_context.md §7. pool_admin_release numeric branch = lib/pool.sh:4394-4420: `if pool_lease_exists "$target"; then pool_release_lane; else 'Lane N has no active lease.' rc 1`. _pool_release_lane_internals (2060-2118) early-returns 0 on an UNREADABLE lease (step (1) at ~2071-2075), so it cannot clean it either — the release path needs its own corrupt-teardown. The kill idiom to reuse: the anchored `user-data-dir=$dir( |$)` cmdline sweep with pkill → sleep 0.2 → pkill -9 (see _pool_release_lane_internals (3b) and pool_reap_orphan_dirs ~3159-3166) — ids from a corrupt lease are untrustworthy by definition.
2. INPUT: from P1.M2.T1.S1 — the reap-side seam is in place (consistent story: corrupt state is reclaimable by BOTH verbs). Interfaces: pool_lease_exists, POOL_LANES_DIR, POOL_EPHEMERAL_ROOT, _pool_log, and the release verb's rc/message contract (0 = released, 1 = nothing to release).
